title: Enterprise Security Enablement Kit refresh (FAQ + one-pagers + RFP library + rollout)
creator: Naomi Feldman
content:
## Context / why this matters
Enterprise deal volume is increasing for Dedicated and Private deployments. Security/compliance review and formal RFPs are gating procurement. Field teams are currently mixing older FAQ language, draft one-pagers, and ad-hoc answers. This creates (a) inconsistencies between deals, (b) avoidable escalations, and (c) risk of over-claiming.

This umbrella ticket refreshes the Enterprise Security Enablement Kit used by Sales, Solutions Engineering, Security/GRC, and Customer Success.

## Goals
1) Publish an up-to-date, canonical Enterprise Security FAQ aligned to current Hosted / Dedicated / Private capabilities.
2) Ship refreshed compliance one-pagers (SOC 2 posture, ISO alignment language, data residency/retention, encryption/KMS, audit logging, SSO/RBAC) with consistent messaging and “do/don’t say” guidance.
3) Standardize an RFP response library with approved language + a maintenance process (versioning, approvals, change log discipline, and a single source of truth).

## Non-goals / explicit constraints
- Do not promise roadmap items. If a control is not supported, use approved alternative language and route to the exceptions policy.
- Do not publish restricted audit evidence broadly; evidence stays gated behind NDA + request workflow.
- Any data residency language must be region-specific and deployment-mode-specific. Avoid “global residency” blanket statements.

## In scope deliverables (customer-facing unless noted)
A) Security FAQ (Confluence, Sales Enablement space)
- Coverage: encryption, data handling, retention/deletion, SSO/SAML/SCIM, RBAC, audit logging, vuln mgmt, incident response, subprocessors, shared responsibility model by deployment mode.
- Includes: “Last reviewed” date, version number, owners, and links to evidence request process.

B) Compliance one-pagers (Drive -> published PDF/Confluence)
- SOC 2 posture one-pager (how to request report under NDA; control themes; scope boundaries)
- ISO 27001 alignment one-pager (approved wording to avoid implying certification)
- Data residency + retention one-pager (regions, data flows, log retention, Dedicated/Private options)
- Encryption + KMS one-pager (in transit/at rest; key ownership boundaries; KMS/HSM options by mode)
- SSO/RBAC + audit logging addendum sections may live as separate one-pagers or as FAQ appendices depending on layout constraints.

C) RFP response library (internal)
- Copy blocks organized by domain: security program, data protection, access controls, audit logging, SDLC, incident response/BCP, subprocessors.
- Each block includes: approved text, evidence availability (green/yellow/red), owner, and link to canonical source.

D) Versioning + maintenance
- Change log and versioning policy (how Sales should cite versions in RFP responses)
- “What we do and don’t say” anti-claims guidance (ISO language, pen-test wording, “no training on customer data” definitions, residency nuance)
- Owners + review cadence (quarterly minimum; ad-hoc on major capability change)

E) Launch & enablement
- Single Confluence index page linking to: FAQ, one-pagers, RFP library, evidence request workflow, owners/SLAs, and escalation path.
- Sales/SE training: how to use kit, common pitfalls, and escalation contacts.
- CRM rollout: update snippets/templates in GTM tools to point at canonical links.

## Target timeline (6–8 weeks)
Week 1–2 (Intake + gap analysis)
- Consolidate top recurring questions from field and support; identify conflicting legacy claims.
- Build initial claims matrix with confidence ratings + evidence mapping.

Week 3–4 (Drafting + claims matrix build)
- Draft FAQ v2026.1 + one-pager drafts.
- Draft RFP library master blocks (v0.9) with owners assigned per section.

Week 5 (Cross-functional review)
- Security Eng + GRC + Product Sec PM review for technical accuracy and audit language.
- Legal/Finance review for any contractual/notification/commitment phrasing.
- Marketing review for messaging consistency and “competitive-safe” wording.

Week 6 (Publish + link updates)
- Publish final artifacts to Confluence; ensure canonical links in the index page.
- Update redwood-docs pages that the kit references (public-friendly wording + evidence request link).

Week 7–8 (Training + rollout)
- Sales enablement session(s) + recording.
- Update HubSpot/CRM snippets/templates and retire older attachments.

## Approvers (RACI for final language)
- Executive sponsor: Dr. Aisha Rahman (final security sign-off)
- Security technical review: Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei
- GRC / compliance language: Olga Petrov, Daniel Carter
- Product capability alignment: Naomi Feldman
- Solutions Engineering validation (mode-specific behavior): Markus Klein, Fatima Noor, Colin O'Donnell
- Legal review (only where commitments/terms appear): Michael Grant
- Commercial packaging alignment (where applicable): Sofia Mendes
- Messaging consistency: Camila Reyes, Soojin Lee
- Docs owner / publishing: Elliot Price

## Key references / linked work
Related tickets
- PM-4829: Standardize RFP response library and approvals
- PM-4860: Update data retention customer language
- ENG-13942: Publish security FAQ to docs site (public-friendly page)
- ENG-13988: Add audit log export docs and examples
- DES-2911: Refresh one-pager templates for compliance
- DES-2924: Visual diagram data flow (Hosted vs Private)

Operational references (canonical locations)
- Evidence request process: SOC 2 / compliance evidence request playbook (NDA-gated)
- Questionnaire exceptions policy (approved alternative language + escalation)
- RFP response ownership and approvals (who can approve deviations)

## Acceptance criteria / launch checklist
Content quality
- FAQ contains deployment-mode-specific answers for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private where behavior differs.
- All claims in FAQ and one-pagers are backed by: (a) existing product behavior, (b) existing policy/process, or (c) explicitly stated as “available upon request / under NDA” for evidence.
- No roadmap promises. Any “planned” language requires Product Sec PM + CISO approval and should be avoided.

Publishing
- Confluence index page exists and is the only page Sales is directed to bookmark.
- Each artifact has: version, last reviewed date, owners, and change log entry (where applicable).
- Public docs (redwood-docs) reference only public-safe language and link to evidence request workflow (no restricted attachments).

Process
- Approved RFP library blocks are stored in the designated location and referenced by GTM snippets.
- Deviations from standard language require review per the RFP approvals SOP.
- Quarterly review meeting is scheduled and owners acknowledged (calendar invite + checklist).

Enablement
- Sales/SE training delivered; recording and slides linked from the index page.
- Old/duplicate attachments in HubSpot are deprecated with pointers to canonical links.

## Risks / open questions
- Data residency wording continues to be a recurring escalation in EMEA; ensure EMEA reviewer (Lukas Meyer) signs off on EU language before publish.
- Audit logging capabilities and export options must match current behavior; coordinate with ENG-13988 + product threads to avoid inconsistencies.
- “No training on customer data” requires precise definition (prompt logging, retention, model improvement). Must use approved language from claims guidance.

## Latest updates
2026-02-24 (Talia)
- Consolidated field intake themes: (1) SOC 2 report access under NDA, (2) EU residency constraints and what is/isn’t configurable, (3) audit log export to SIEM and event field list, (4) SSO/SCIM coverage for console vs API, (5) encryption/KMS boundaries for Private deployments.
- Confirmed review sequence: Security Eng -> GRC -> Product Sec PM -> Legal (as needed) -> Marketing -> final CISO sign-off.
- Blocker noted: final one-pager templates and data-flow diagram needed to lock layout; tracking via DES-2911 and DES-2924.

2026-02-10 (Naomi)
- Reiterated non-goal: do not introduce new product commitments; if a control is not supported, route through exceptions policy and include best-available alternative language.
- Requested that RFP blocks include explicit scope boundaries (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) to reduce back-and-forth in security questionnaires.
